The angular distribution from and of scattered protons were measured for incident proton energies of 600, 700, 800, and 990 keV. “Measurement of the scattering of protons by deuterium, helium, and air, together with “vacuum-scattering” tests which eliminate slit scattering and unknown vapors, have led to the conclusion that the observed anomaly is not due to a contamination and must be ascribed to a proton-proton interaction at close distances (less that 13cm) which involves a marked departure from the ordinary Coulomb forces.” The theoretical inter pretation was presented by Breit et al. in an accompanying paper (1936Br07).
